parsed.summary: Two statements are formalized. (1) euler_breakdown_R3: some smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u₀ on ℝ³ admits no global smooth unforced Euler solution (v,p) on [0,∞) with L² velocity and uniformly bounded energy. (2) exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity: there is a nonzero compactly supported such u₀ and a T* ∈ (0,1] with a smooth Sobolev-class solution on [0,T*); closed-interval Sobolev solutions exist exactly for T < T*; the C¹ norm is bounded and the time integral of sup|ω| is finite on shorter intervals; at T* the limsup of the C¹ norm and ∫₀^{T*}‖ω‖_∞ dt are both infinite; and the same datum has no global solution. Most important caveat: the blow-up clause uses ‖u‖_∞+‖∇u‖_∞ rather than ‖∇u‖_∞ alone, so it is formally slightly weaker than the paper's lim sup ‖∇u‖_∞ = ∞. Separately, the 'finite energy' clause is vacuous.

glossary.note: Junk value 0 only where v is not differentiable; every use is on smooth fields.

glossary.plain: In addition, every derivative satisfies |D^m u₀(x)| ≤ C_{m,K}(1+|x|)^{-K}
glossary.note: Implied by compact support plus smoothness.

glossary.plain: (v,p) is C^∞ on ℝ³×[0,∞), satisfies ∂ₜv + (v·∇)v = −∇p and ∇·v = 0 for t ≥ 0, with v(·,0) = u₀
glossary.note: The one-sided derivative at t = 0 is a harmless convention.

glossary.plain: The global smooth solution above, with v(t) ∈ L² for each t and sup_t ‖v(t)‖₂² finite
glossary.standard_concept: Clay whole-space smooth finite-energy solution class
glossary.note: Extra requirements only weaken the nonexistence claim; this is the standard Clay class.

glossary.plain: The L² class of f, or 0 if f ∉ L²
glossary.note: The fallback is guarded by MemLp hypotheses at every use.

glossary.plain: For t ∈ I, v(t) is C^∞ and every jet D^m v(t) is in L², continuous in t in L²
On the time set I: div-free, v(0) = u₀, v ∈ C(I;H^∞), p spatially differentiable at interior times; v has a strong L² time derivative w ∈ C(I;H^∞) with w + (v·∇)v = −∇p pointwise at interior times
glossary.standard_concept: classical H^∞ Euler solution on I
glossary.note: Pressure has no time regularity; fine for defining the lifespan.
The paper's blow-up quantity is ‖∇u‖_∞ alone.

lean_claims.plain: ∃ u₀ smooth, div-free, with all derivatives rapidly decaying, such that there is no (v,p) C^∞ on ℝ³×[0,∞) solving unforced Euler with v(0) = u₀, v(t) ∈ L² for all t, and uniformly bounded energy.

∃ u₀, T*, v, p such that: u₀ is smooth, div-free, decaying, compactly supported and nonzero; 0 < T* ≤ 1; (v,p) is an H^∞ Euler solution on [0,T*); [vacuous] some time has finite energy; for every T > 0, an H^∞ solution on [0,T] exists iff T < T*; for T < T*, sup_{[0,T]} (‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞) < ∞ and ∫₀^T ‖ω‖_∞ < ∞; limsup_{t↑T*} (‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞) = ∞; ∫₀^{T*} ‖ω‖_∞ dt = ∞; and u₀ has no global solution in the class EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3.

paper_claims.plain: There exists u₀ ∈ C_c^∞ div-free on ℝ³ with 0 < T*(u₀) < ∞, whose smooth solution satisfies lim sup_{t↑T*} ‖∇u(t)‖_∞ = ∞ and ∫₀^{T*} ‖curl u‖_∞ dt = ∞.

coverage.why: Matches up to (a) the C¹ norm including ‖u‖_∞ (formally weaker), (b) extra stronger clauses (T* ≤ 1, maximality iff, global nonexistence), and (c) T* defined via the H^∞ class.
Nonexistence of a global Clay-class solution is a consequence of finite-time blow-up; it is not an explicit claim in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: The limsup blow-up is stated for ‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞, not ‖∇v‖_∞. Formally this is weaker: it would also hold if only ‖v‖_∞ blew up. For Euler this cannot happen (by BKM and energy-type arguments), and the vorticity clause independently pins the singularity.
flags.probe_idea: Replace with Filter.limsup (fun t => ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ (v · t) x‖) (𝓝[<] Tstar) = ⊤

flags.explanation: The clause ∃ E, ∃ t ∈ [0,T*), ∫|v(t)|² < E is trivially true (take t = 0 and E = integral+1). The docstring's 'finite-energy' claim is vacuous. The paper excerpt does not claim it.
flags.probe_idea: Prove the clause trivially with t = 0, E = (∫ ‖v x 0‖^2) + 1

flags.explanation: v is existentially chosen rather than being 'the' solution; uniqueness is not asserted. This is harmless given uniqueness in the H^∞ class, but formally it only asserts some solution blows up as stated.
flags.probe_idea: Add uniqueness: ∀ w q, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Ico 0 Tstar) u₀ w q → ∀ t ∈ Ico 0 Tstar, (w · t) = (v · t)

flags.explanation: lintegral of a possibly non-measurable t ↦ sup_x|ω| is a lower integral. The finiteness claim at line 180 could be weaker if the map were non-measurable; continuity in H^∞ makes it measurable in practice.
flags.probe_idea: Measurable (fun t => vorticityNorm (v · t)) on Ico 0 Tstar
